subject: HealthBridge discovery — model-fit gaps + streaming UX follow-ups

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@healthbridge.com>, Sandeep Rao <sandeep@medgrid.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: HealthBridge discovery — model-fit gaps + streaming UX follow-ups

Jordan / Sandeep — thanks again for the call yesterday. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

What we heard
- Primary use: real-time patient triage assistant embedded in clinician UI (short prompts, few-shot context, must avoid hallucination).
- SLOs: 95th perc latency target ~250ms token-level (interactive feel), end-to-end completion under 1.2s for typical 40-token responses.
- Key concern: partial/fragmented outputs when streaming (stop sequences not respected sometimes) and occasional incoherent mid-stream continuations.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Pilot eval: run a small benchmark (50 representative prompts you provided) against 3 model candidates and streaming config variants. I attached a prompt set (hb_prompt_set_v1.txt).
2) Benchmark artifacts: we’ll share a CSV of token latency and coherence flags; provisional results attached (streaming-bench-20261119.csv).
3) Engineering sync: Marissa + Karthik will propose model variants, prompt/stop-sequence patterns, and a canary rollout plan for streaming.
4) Follow-up meeting: 30 minutes next week to review results and pick the model+deployment (hosted vs. dedicated).

Recommended starting models (initial guess) — we’ll validate in bench: 
- redwood-instruct-medium-v1 (latency-friendly, stronger instruction following)
- rw-13b-q4f (higher quality, quantized for cost)
- open-llama-7b-instruct (baseline comparison)

Known risks we’ll watch for in the pilot
- Stop-sequence enforcement with partial flushes during streaming.
- Early termination behaviors when client interrupts or network blips occur.
- Quality regressions when using aggressive quantization or smaller context kernels.

Attachments: hb_prompt_set_v1.txt (prompt samples), discovery-recording-20261119.mp4 (call), streaming-bench-20261119.csv (preliminary).

If that plan looks good, Jordan — can you confirm the 50 prompts in the attached file are the right set for the clinician flows (or point to updated set) and confirm a good time for the sync next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — scope looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Yes, the attached prompt set is a good start; I'll add 5 more edge-case prompts (no PII) and send an updated file by Monday.
- The streaming problem: clinicians report seeing 'partial sentences' where the model emits a fragment and then later repeats or contradicts itself mid-stream. This seems particularly bad with multi-turn prompts where we include a short patient history.
- Latency note: 250ms token at 95th is ambitious; our primary ask is perceived interactivity (sub-1s feels real-time). If you can demonstrate consistent <300ms token for the mid-tier model that would be convincing.

Can you include recommended stop-sequence recipes in the bench (for example, how we structure the finish tokens and whether to use client-side buffer timeouts)? Also need a sample of what the streaming partial output looks like (with timestamps) so our frontend can implement retry/fallback behavior.

I’m available Wed 11/25 10:00–11:30 PT or Thu 11/26 13:00–14:00 PT for the follow-up.

Ben / team / Jordan — quick technical notes from the bench POV. High level recommendations and immediate actions below.

Short summary
- Best tradeoff for initial pilot: redwood-instruct-medium-v1 with streaming params tuned (lower prefetch, ensure stop-token enforcement on server-side). rw-13b-q4f showed better static-quality but is brittle under aggressive batching and quantization for low-latency streaming.

Technical findings (internal run against hb_prompt_set_v1.txt, avg context 120 tokens)
- redwood-instruct-medium-v1: median token latency ~85ms, 95th ~220ms when running with batch size 8 and kv-cache enabled (on a c5-like config). Stop-seq honored in 98% of samples with server-side enforcement and trailing flush delay of 40ms.
- rw-13b-q4f: median token latency ~150ms, 95th ~360ms; quality uplift ~7% on hallucination metrics but stop-seq dropped to 92% under heavy concurrent streams.
- open-llama-7b-instruct: fast but higher hallucination risk on clinical prompts; not recommended for pilot.

Stop-sequence recommendations for streaming UX
- Server-side canonical enforcement: include both model-generated EOS and a client-side sentinel (e.g., "<END_NOTE>") as stop tokens. Server should flush the KV buffer and send finalization marker.
- Trailing flush timeout: 30–50ms works well to avoid chopping final tokens while keeping perceived latency low.
- Client-side buffering: keep a 100–150ms soft buffer; present partial tokens incrementally but delay rendering the last 1–2 tokens until finalization to avoid mid-stream contradictions.

Canary / rollout plan
1) Internal bench results -> share CSV + short write-up (Tue morning). 
2) Canary: 5% of HealthBridge traffic routed to tuned redwood-instruct-medium-v1 streaming config with server-side stop enforcement + client buffer flag. Monitor coherence KPI and token-latency for 48 hours.
3) If coherence regressions <1.5% and 95th token latency <300ms, expand to 25% and then 100% over 72 hours. Fail/rollback if regressions spike or if errors >1%.

Action items (owners)
- Karthik: run full bench on rw-13b-q4f vs redwood-instruct-medium-v1 with the edge prompts Jordan will add; include quantization settings and exact hardware used. Deliverable: bench CSV + a short note on where stop-seq failures occurred. (Due: Tue 11/24 EOD).
- Ben: confirm pilot scope with Jordan and lock the follow-up slot (Wed or Thu).
- Marissa: prepare the canary runbook and monitoring dashboard (coherence, token latency, error rate).

I’ll attach a short example of a streamed partial-output (with timestamps) in the drive folder and add the stop-seq recipes to the bench report.
